title: bug: claim_next_task and release_task run their disk-state git status (up to 3 s) under the global state mutex: neither is marked blocking, so McpAdapter wraps the whole handler and every tool fleet-wide stalls behind the subprocess that diskState.ts says must run outside the lock
description:
Found by defect hunt #13 (task-cc441586). Line numbers are at HEAD f159784e.

PROBLEM
- util/diskState.ts:19-22 states the rule (invariant 2): "Callers MUST invoke this OUTSIDE the state mutex. It spawns a git subprocess that can take up to the 3s timeout; ... running it under the lock would freeze every tool fleet-wide".
- Both callers were written to follow it:
  - tools/releaseTask.ts:178-191 captures the handoff fingerprint in a "pre-mutex region ... never inside runExclusive" (computeDiskStateSignature at :186). Its own state.runExclusive starts at :194.
  - tools/claimNextTask.ts:422-424 says the recompute "must never run under the global state mutex". Its runExclusive is at :429, and the post-mutex recompute is at :1008-1019 ("The mutex is released — safe to shell out to git").
- Neither tool sets `blocking: true`. So server/McpAdapter.ts:309 (`tool.blocking ? await invoke() : await this.state.runExclusive(invoke)`) wraps the WHOLE handler. The mutex is reentrant, so it stays held through the git call.
- `blocking` is read only at McpAdapter.ts:309. The dispatch comment at :301-303 still calls claim_next_task "safe to wrap".
- The transports disagree: /ws RELEASE_TASK (server/WebSocketServer.ts:723-740) calls the same handler with no wrapper, so the capture runs unlocked there as intended.
- Precedent: submit_plan opts out the same way for its bounded cached-Git lookup (tools/submitPlan.ts:198 `blocking: true`; packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md:5).

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cc441586/B/diskStateUnderMutex.test.ts. Copy it into packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive f159784e` snapshot.
- It mocks computeDiskStateSignature with a 600 ms git stand-in, records state.mutex.isHeld() during it, and times a bystander moe.list_tasks.
- Command: `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/diskStateUnderMutex.test.ts`. Result: 2 failed. Verbatim:
```
release_task: mutex held during git = [ true ] ; bystander list_tasks waited 567 ms
claim_next_task: mutex held during git = [ true ] ; bystander list_tasks waited 571 ms
× release_task with a handoffNote: git runs outside the mutex and does not stall other tools
× claim_next_task of a task whose newest handoff carries a diskState: git runs outside the mutex
AssertionError: expected [ true ] to deeply equal [ false ]
```
- Exposure:
  - Every MCP release_task that carries a handoffNote stalls all tool dispatch and /ws mutations for as long as git runs, up to the 3 s kill.
  - The board holds 18 handoff notes and none carries a diskState, so every capture so far failed or timed out.
  - `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch` took 4.35 s from WSL over /mnt/d. The live daemon runs on Windows, so that timing is indicative only.
  - The claim-side stall stays dormant until a stored diskState exists.

FIX DIRECTION
- Mark moe.claim_next_task and moe.release_task `blocking: true`, the submit_plan precedent. Both already do every state read-modify-write inside their own state.runExclusive:
  - claim_next_task's handler (:421) has no await before :429 and writes nothing after it;
  - release_task does only validation and the capture before :194.
- Update the McpAdapter dispatch comment (:301-303) and the blocking-tools list in packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md:5.
- Never move the capture into the mutex.
- docs/MCP_SERVER.md is held at filing time: sync it only if lanes show it free at planning time.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/{claimNextTask,releaseTask}.ts, src/server/McpAdapter.ts (dispatch comment hunk only, ~:301-303; sibling hunt row on the rate limiter owns the env/RateLimiter hunks at ~:15-56), packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md, plus a new vitest file.
definitionOfDone: Through MCP dispatch, release_task's handoff disk-state capture and claim_next_task's post-claim recompute run with state.mutex.isHeld() false, and a bystander moe.list_tasks sent during a slow (mocked) capture returns before the capture ends, in a new vitest file.

Every claim and release mutation still runs inside the tool's own state.runExclusive (the existing claimNextTask and releaseTask tests pass unchanged), and the McpAdapter dispatch comment and packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md's blocking-tools list name both tools.
`npx vitest run` of the new file plus src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts and src/tools/releaseTask.test.ts passes in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
Verification, run once (see mem:convention-daemon-vitest-mutant-checkref).

Run the GREEN checkRef (the execution contract's first) verbatim; it is complete_task's verification. It does the following:
- archives HEAD's packages/moe-daemon, scripts, docs and CLAUDE.md into a mktemp snapshot and overlays your five files;
- runs npm ci there, then typechecks the sources (`tsc --noEmit`) and the new test file (`tt.json`);
- runs the new file, every claimNextTask suite, releaseTask.test.ts (both unchanged, DoD 2), McpAdapter.test.ts and daemonGitDocs.test.ts (the edited comments and CLAUDE.md);
- runs every suite that drives claim or release through McpAdapter: src/delivery, src/__acceptance__, workstreamComposition, dependencyUnblock and submitPlan.
It is a superset of DoD 3's three files. In the architect's dry run (09529122 plus this plan) it exited 0 with `Test Files  34 passed (34)` and `Tests  1643 passed (1643)`, about 12 s of tests after npm ci. The counts move only if a peer adds tests to those suites.

Then run the RED checkRef once more. It must still print RED-AT-BASE. Quote both outputs in your completion summary.

Error handling for a red run:
- A failure in the new file: fix the source, never the assertions. The test is the DoD's evidence.
- A failure in any other suite: re-run it in a second snapshot without your overlay (`git archive HEAD` only).
  - If it fails there too, it is pre-existing. Do not edit it: post the evidence in #general and call moe.report_blocked.
  - If it fails only with your change, fix your change. Never weaken a test.

Optional, not part of the gate: in the architect's dry run, the whole daemon suite in a whole-tree snapshot (`git archive HEAD | tar -x`) passed with this change: 270 files, 7350 passed, 24 skipped.

Leave nothing in the checkout or the worktree. The snapshots live in /tmp.

Adversarial self-review (load adversarial-self-review) of your `git diff`. Fix any finding, then re-run step 4's two checkRefs.

(1) Scope:
- claimNextTask.ts and releaseTask.ts gain only the comment and `blocking: true`;
- McpAdapter.ts only the dispatch comment hunk;
- packages/moe-daemon/CLAUDE.md one sentence;
- plus the new test.
No handler logic changed, the existing claim and release test files are untouched, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md is unchanged.

(2) Lock coverage:
- claim: still no await before its runExclusive, and nothing after it except the recompute and the reply;
- release: every gate and write is inside runExclusive, which re-reads the row with state.getTask;
- outside the two runExclusive blocks, the handlers touch state only through the synchronous role read and state.projectPath.

(3) Concurrency, now that dispatch no longer serializes these two tools:
- Two claims racing for one row still serialize on the claim's own runExclusive, and one wins.
- A release with a handoffNote now queues for the lock after its git call, so a tool sent during the capture runs first. A claim in that window still sees the row assigned and skips it. The release's TASK_UPDATED then wakes any parked wait_for_task seat.

(4) Known residual, by design; state it in the completion summary. release_task's force role check runs before the lock, as it already did on /ws, whose RELEASE_TASK calls the handler unwrapped. A team-role change that races a force release is therefore judged on the role at call time.

(5) Wire: unchanged. tools/list exposes only name, description and inputSchema, both reply shapes are identical, and moe-proxy is untouched.

Then call moe.complete_task with step 4's GREEN evidence.

A moe.list_tasks sent while either is parked answers before it ends (diskStateDispatch.test.ts (d1), (d2)).

Every updateTask/updateWorker call those claims and releases make runs with state.mutex.isHeld() true. The release stores the captured signature on priorHandoffs[0].diskState, and the claim reports staleHandoffDiskState: true.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: mark both tools `blocking: true`, the precedent set by submit_plan (tools/submitPlan.ts:198) and get_execution_readiness (:103). Both handlers already do every state read-modify-write inside their own state.runExclusive, so only the dispatch wrap has to go. Rejected:
(a) Releasing the lock inside the handler around the git call. AsyncMutex.exit() only leaves the AsyncLocalStorage context; it does not release a lock the outer wrap holds, so other tools would still queue. A real unlock-and-relock helper would be a new mechanism for what the flag already expresses.
(b) Moving the capture into the lock, or dropping it. That violates util/diskState.ts invariant 2 and the row's fix direction.
(c) Marking only release_task. The claim-side stall goes live as soon as any stored diskState exists.
(d) Editing the ToolDefinition.blocking JSDoc in tools/index.ts. Its example list is non-exhaustive and still true.
(e) Syncing docs/MCP_SERVER.md. Neither contract changes, and its release_task section already says the capture runs outside the state mutex (true after this fix). A 6th file would also floor the plan to the heavy tier, because the size rule counts newFiles.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- server/McpAdapter.ts:309 is the only production reader of ToolDefinition.blocking. tools/list exposes only name, description and inputSchema, so the flag is not on the wire.
- Three test helpers mirror the dispatch rule: executionPolicyLifecycle.test.ts:163, profileRollout.test.ts:111 and getExecutionReadiness.test.ts:72.
- moe-proxy's BLOCKING_LONG_POLLS (index.ts:273) is a separate, hard-coded long-poll timeout list. It already omits submit_plan and get_execution_readiness.
- WebSocketServer RELEASE_TASK (:723-740) calls the release handler unwrapped.
- AsyncMutex (state/StateManager.ts:268) is reentrant via AsyncLocalStorage. isHeld() reports whether the calling async context is inside runExclusive, and StateManager.mutex is public readonly.
- util/daemonGitDocs.test.ts scans every CLAUDE.md, every docs/*.md file and every non-test daemon source line for /never (?:runs|executes|touches) git|runs no git|does not run git/i.
- Architect dry run at 09529122, with this exact plan applied in a scratch clone: both checkRefs passed verbatim (GREEN 34 files / 1643 tests; RED printed RED-AT-BASE). The whole daemon suite in a whole-tree snapshot passed 270 files, 7350 passed, 24 skipped.
planningNotes.risks:
1) Never add an await before claim_next_task's runExclusive. Today the claim takes the lock synchronously on entry, so claim ordering is unchanged; an await would let a later call go first.
2) A release with a handoffNote now queues for the lock after its git call, so tools sent during the capture go first. This is benign: a claim in that window still sees the row assigned.
3) release_task's force role check (workerHasRole, a synchronous read) runs before the lock, as it already does on /ws. A team-role change that races a force release is judged on the role at call time. This is a known residual, by design.
4) Comments and CLAUDE.md must avoid the NEVER_RUNS_GIT phrases that daemonGitDocs checks.
5) The RED checkRef pins exactly two cases with the (d1) and (d2) prefixes.
6) Leave McpAdapter's env/RateLimiter hunks alone: open row task-301cf760 owns them.
